text:
maya: heads-up — midnight perf dashboard just flared. p99 for text-gen (canary) up ~26% after the merge we rolled at 22:50 (PR#4821). https://dash.redwood/internal/alerts/4460012345 :eyes:

rachel: link? i'm seeing cluster util normal but tail latency spike on the per-model panel. looks concentrated on gpu-pool-a canary nodes.

jun: digging — PR#4821 touched kernel-selector heuristics. changed default path for sequences >512 from `execpath-v2` -> `perf-est` (aim was throughput win). quick diff:```diff
- default_kernel = "execpath-v2"
+ default_kernel = "perf-est"
```

liam: any CI signals? did nightly bench show this earlier? @ci-bot

ci-bot: nightly-gpu-bench (2026-03-17 23:40:12) — job: gpu-bench/text-gen — status: FAILED (regression detected)
  summary: p99 increased 18% vs baseline
  failing-test: bench/latency/p99
  logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/98765/logs

jun: okay that aligns. PR passed unit/e2e but the microbenchmark flagged ~18% and the rollout still went — looks like the alert thresholds didn't block. suspect heuristic flip caused less efficient kernel selection for our long-tail sequences -> KV cache patterns changed and we lost batching locality.

maya: can we pause canary and run a quick revert? we need fast mitigation while we bisect.

rachel: deploying pause to rollout for that model group now. @deploy-bot pause rollout canary gpu-pool-a PR#4821

deploy-bot: rollout paused for group=canary gpu-pool-a (actioned by rachel). current canary traffic frozen at 12:07am.

liam: i'll open a revert PR (restore default_kernel to execpath-v2) and drive canary rollback. assigning to myself.

jun: in parallel i'll do a narrow bisect: reproduce locally with the benchmark harness + perf traces. steps i'm running:
  1) checkout merge-base before PR#4821
  2) run bench/latency/p99 with `--seq 768 --concurrency 8`
  3) capture `perf record` and our runtime `kv-stats` output
  quick perf snippet from failing run:
```
  runtime: select_kernel=perf-est
  kv-cache: miss_rate=0.17, cold_evictions=9
  batch-coalesce: avg_size=3.2 (expected ~5.4)
  p99=132ms (baseline p99=105ms)
```

maya: good data. the batch-coalesce drop + KV miss uplift look like a behavior change from the selector (it picks a kernel that doesn't preserve batching affinity?).

jun: yep. preliminary local diff shows `perf-est` emits a slightly different prefetch schedule which fragments the request stream -> smaller batches -> worse tail. i'm confident PR#4821 is the primary culprit but will finish bisect to be safe.

liam: revert PR created: https://git.redwood/reverts/revert-4821. tagging @oncall and @eng-runtime. will request canary rollback once CI passes.

ci-bot: revert-4821 — CI bench queued. nightly-gpu-bench baseline run scheduled.

jun: if revert fixes it we should consider a follow-up that keeps perf-est but gates it behind a rollout flag and adds a stricter microbench block. also add a regression alert hook that blocks merges when p99 reg >10% in nightly-bench.

maya: agreed. owners: liam -> rollback+revert PR, jun -> bisect+investigate prefetch schedule change, rachel -> monitor canary and confirm rollback effects. i'll own follow-up with gating/alerting.

liam: rolling back canary once CI green, will update thread. :thumbsup:

rachel: monitoring charts, will post p99 after rollback.

jun: note for postmortem — add a perf-test variant with seq distribution skewed to long-tail to catch this class of regression.

ci-bot: nightly-gpu-bench (revert-4821) — PASS (prelim). p99 back within 2% of baseline.

liam: rollback initiated, canary now at previous model commit.

rachel: confirmed p99 dropped back to baseline on gpu-pool-a. closing immediate incident.

maya: thanks team. follow-up actions: 1) gated rollout flag for perf-est, 2) stricter bench-block in CI, 3) add long-tail seq test to nightly harness. jun/maya/rachel to own.

jun: i'll start on the perf-est rollback patch and tests tomorrow.

liam: closing thread after PR merge.

maya: :white_check_mark:
